Central quotient versus commutator subgroup of groups

Manoj K. Yadav Address: School of Mathematics, Harish-Chandra Research Institute
Chhatnag Road, Jhunsi, Allahabad - 211 019, INDIA Email address: myadav@hri.res.in
Abstract.

In 1904, Issai Schur proved the following result. If GG is an arbitrary group such that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite, where Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G) denotes the center of the group GG, then the commutator subgroup of GG is finite. A partial converse of this result was proved by B. H. Neumann in 1951. He proved that if GG is a finitely generated group with finite commutator subgroup, then G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite. In this short note, we exhibit few arguments of Neumann, which provide further generalizations of converse of the above mentioned result of Schur. We classify all finite groups GG such that |G/Z⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d}, where dd denotes the number of elements in a minimal generating set for G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G). Some problems and questions are posed in the sequel.

Key words and phrases: 
commutator subgroup, Schur’s theorem, class-preserving automorphism
2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 20F24, 20E45

1. Introduction

In 1951, Neumann [18, Theorem 5.3] proved the following result: If the index of Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G) in GG is finite, then γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, where Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G) and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) denote the center and the commutator subgroup of GG respectively. He mentioned [19, End of page 237] that this result can be obtained from an implicit idea of Schur [23], and his proof also used Schur’s basic idea. However there is no mention of this fact in [18] in which Schur’s paper is also cited. In this note, this result will be termed as ‘the Schur’s theorem’. Neumann also provided a partial converse of the Schur’s theorem [18, Corollary 5.41] as follows: If GG is finitely generated by kk elements and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, then G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite, and bounded by |G/Z⁡(G)|≤|γ2​(G)|k|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{k}.

Our first motivation of writing this note is to exhibit an idea of Neumann[18, page 179] which proves much more than what is said above on converse of the Schur’s theorem. We quote the text here (with a minor modification in the notations):

“Let GG be generated by g1,g2,…,gkg_{1},g_{2},\ldots,g_{k}. Then

Z(G)=∩κ=1κ=kCG(gκ);\operatorname{Z}(G)=\cap_{\kappa=1}^{\kappa=k}C_{G}(g_{\kappa});

for, an element of GG lies in the centre if and only if it (is permutable) commutes with all the generators of GG. If GG is an FC-group (group whose all conjugacy classes are of finite length), then |G:CG(gκ)||G:C_{G}(g_{\kappa})| is finite for 1≤κ≤k1\leq\kappa\leq k, and Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G), as intersection of a finite set of subgroups of finite index, also has finite index. The index of the intersection of two subgroups does not exceed the product of the indices of the subgroups: hence in this case one obtains an upper bound for the index of the centre, namely

|G:Z(G)|≤Πκ=1κ=k|G:CG(gκ)|."|G:\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq\Pi_{\kappa=1}^{\kappa=k}|G:C_{G}(g_{\kappa})|."

Just a soft staring at the quoted text for a moment or two suggests the following. The conclusion does not require the group GG to be FC-group. It only requires the finiteness of the conjugacy classes of the generating elements. If a generator of the group GG is contained in Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G), one really does not need to count it. Thus the argument works perfactly well even if GG is generated by infinite number of elements, all but finite of them lie in the center of GG. Thus the following result holds true.

Theorem A.

Let GG be an arbitrary group such that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finitely generated by x1​Z⁡(G),x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G), x2​Z⁡(G),x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(G), …,xt​Z⁡(G)\ldots,x_{t}\operatorname{Z}(G) and the conjugacy class of xix_{i} in GG is of finite length for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Then G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite. Moreover |G/Z⁡(G)|≤Πi=1t​|xiG||G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|x_{i}^{G}| and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, where xiGx_{i}^{G} denotes the conjugacy class of xix_{i} in GG.

Neumann’s result [18, Corollary 5.41] was reproduced by Hilton [12, Theorem 1]. It seems that Hilton was not aware of Neumann’s result. This lead two more publications [21] and [24] dedicated to proving special cases of Theorem A.

Converse of the Schur’s theorem is not true in general as shown by infinite extraspecial pp-groups, where pp is an odd prime. It is interesting to know that example of such a 22-group also exists, which is mentioned on page 238 (second para of Section 3) of [19]. It is a central product of infinite copies of quaternion groups of order 88 amalgamated at the center of order 22.

Our second motivation of writing this note is to provide a modification of an innocent looking result of Neumann [20, Lemma 2], which allows us to say little more on converse of the Schur’s theorem. A modified version of this lemma is the following.

Lemma 1.1.

Let GG be an arbitrary group having a normal abelian subgroup AA such that the index of CG​(A)C_{G}(A) in GG is finite and G/AG/A is finitely generated by g1​A,g2​A,…,gr​Ag_{1}A,g_{2}A,\ldots,g_{r}A, where |giG|<∞|g_{i}^{G}|<\infty for 1≤i≤r1\leq i\leq r. Then G/Z⁡(G)G/Z(G) is finite.

This lemma helps proving the first three statements of the following result.

Theorem B.

For an arbitrary group GG, G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite if any one of the following holds true:

(i) Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)) is finitely generated and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite.

(ii) G/Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))G/\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)) is finitely generated and G/(Z2⁡(G)​γ2​(G))G/(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)\gamma_{2}(G)) is finite.

(iii) γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite and Z2⁡(G)≤γ2​(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)\leq\gamma_{2}(G).

(iv) γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite and G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is purely non-abelian.

Our final motivation is to provide a classification of all groups GG upto isoclinism (see Section 3 for the definition) such that |G/Z⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d} is finite, where dd denotes the number of elements in a minimal generating set for G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G), discuss example in various situations and pose some problems. We conclude this section with fixing some notations. For an arbitrary group GG, by Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G), Z2⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) we denote the center, the second center and the commutator subgroup of GG respectively. For x∈Gx\in G, [x,G][x,G] denotes the set {[x,g]∣g∈G}\{[x,g]\mid g\in G\}. Notice that |[x,G]|=|xG||[x,G]|=|x^{G}|, where xGx^{G} denotes the conjugacy class of xx in GG. If [x,G]⊆Z⁡(G)[x,G]\subseteq\operatorname{Z}(G), then [x,G][x,G] becomes a subgroup of GG. For a subgroup HH of GG, CG⁡(H)\operatorname{C}_{G}(H) denotes the centralizer of HH in GG and for an element x∈Gx\in G, CG⁡(x)\operatorname{C}_{G}(x) denotes the centralizer of xx in GG.

2. Proofs

We start with the proof of Lemma 1.1, which is essentialy same as the one given by Neumann.

Proof of Lemma 1.1. Let G/AG/A be generated by g1​A,g2​A,…,gr​Ag_{1}A,g_{2}A,\ldots,g_{r}A for some gi∈Gg_{i}\in G, where 1≤i≤r<∞1\leq i\leq r<\infty. Let X:={g1,g2,…,gr}X:=\{g_{1},g_{2},\ldots,g_{r}\} and AA be generated by a set YY. Then G=⟨X∪Y⟩G=\left<X\cup Y\right> and Z⁡(G)=CG⁡(X)∩CG​(Y)\operatorname{Z}(G)=\operatorname{C}_{G}(X)\cap C_{G}(Y). Notice that CG​(A)=CG​(Y)C_{G}(A)=C_{G}(Y). Since CG​(A)C_{G}(A) is of finite index, CG​(Y)C_{G}(Y) is also of finite index in GG. Also, since |giG|<∞|g_{i}^{G}|\ <\infty for 1≤i≤r1\leq i\leq r, CG​(X)C_{G}(X) is of finite index in GG. Hence the index of Z⁡(G)Z(G) in GG is finite and the proof is complete. □\Box

Proof of Theorem A can be made quite precise by using Lemma 1.1.

Proof of Theorem A. Taking A=Z⁡(G)A=\operatorname{Z}(G) in Lemma 1.1, it follows that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite. Moreover,

|G/Z(G)|=|G/∩i=1tCG(xi)|≤Πi=1t|G:CG(xi)|=Πi=1t|[xi,G]|=Πi=1t|xiG|.|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|G/\cap_{i=1}^{t}C_{G}(x_{i})|\leq\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|G:C_{G}(x_{i})|=\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|[x_{i},G]|=\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|x_{i}^{G}|.

That γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite now follows from the Schur’s theorem. □\Box

For the proof of Theorem B we need the following result of Hall [9] and the subsequent proposition.

Theorem 2.1.

If GG is an arbitrary group such that γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, then G/Z2⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) is finite.

Explicit bounds on the order of G/Z2⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) were first given by Macdonald [14, Theorem 6.2] and later on improved by Podoski and Szegedy [22] by showing that if |γ2​(G)/(γ2​(G)∩Z⁡(G))|=n|\gamma_{2}(G)/(\gamma_{2}(G)\cap\operatorname{Z}(G))|=n, then |G/Z2⁡(G)|≤nc​l​o​g2​n|G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)|\leq n^{c\;log_{2}n} with c=2c=2.

Proposition 2.2.

Let GG be an arbitrary group such that γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite and G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is infinite. Then G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) has an infinite abelian group as a direct factor.

Proof.

Since γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, by Theorem 2.1 G/Z2⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) is finite. Thus Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is infinite. Again using the finiteness of γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G), it follows that the exponent of Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite. Hence by [6, Theorem 17.2] Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is a direct sum of cyclic groups. Let G/Z2⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) be generated by x1​Z2⁡(G),…,xr​Z2⁡(G)x_{1}\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G),\ldots,x_{r}\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) and H:=⟨x1,…,xr⟩H:=\left<x_{1},\ldots,x_{r}\right>. Then it follows that modulo Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G), H∩Z2⁡(G)H\cap\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) is finite. Thus we can write

Z2(G)/Z(G)=⟨y1Z(G)⟩×⋯×⟨ysZ(G)⟩×⟨ys+1Z(G)⟩×⋯,\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)=\left<y_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>\times\cdots\times\left<y_{s}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>\times\left<y_{s+1}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>\times\cdots,

such that (H∩Z2(G))Z(G)/Z(G)≤⟨y1Z(G)⟩×⋯×⟨ysZ(G)⟩(H\cap\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G))\operatorname{Z}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)\leq\left<y_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>\times\cdots\times\left<y_{s}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>. It now follows that the infinite abelian group ⟨ys+1Z(G)⟩×⋯\left<y_{s+1}\operatorname{Z}(G)\right>\times\cdots is a direct factor of G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G), and the proof is complete. □\Box

∎

We are now ready to prove Theorem B.

Proof of Theorem B. Since γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite, it follows from Theorem 2.1 that G/Z2⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) is finite. Now using the fact that Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)) is finitely generated, it follows that G/Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))G/\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)) is finitely generated. Take Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))=A\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G))=A. Then notice that AA is a normal abelian subgroup of GG such that the index of CG​(A)C_{G}(A) in GG is finite, since Z2⁡(G)≤CG​(A)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)\leq C_{G}(A). Hence by Lemma 1.1, G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite, which proves (i).

Again take Z⁡(Z2⁡(G))=A\operatorname{Z}(\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G))=A and notice that Z2⁡(G)​γ2​(G)≤CG⁡(A)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)\gamma_{2}(G)\leq\operatorname{C}_{G}(A). (ii) now directly follows from Lemma 1.1. If Z2⁡(G)≤γ2​(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)\leq\gamma_{2}(G), then Z2⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) is abelian. Thus (iii) follows from (i). Finally, (iv) follows from Proposition 2.2. This completes the proof of the theorem. □\Box

We conclude this section with an extension of Theorem A in terms of conjugacy class-preserving automorphisms of given group GG. An automorphism α\alpha of an arbitrary group GG is called (conjugacy) class-preserving if α⁡(g)∈gG\alpha(g)\in g^{G} for all g∈Gg\in G. We denote the group of all class-preserving automorphisms of GG by Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G). Notice that Inn⁡(G)\operatorname{Inn}(G), the group of all inner automorphisms of GG, is a normal subgroup of Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G) and Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G) acts trivially on the center of GG. A detailed survey on class-preserving automorphisms of finite pp-groups can be found in [25].

Let GG be the group as in the statement of Theorem A. Then GG is generated by x1,x2,…,xtx_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{t} along with Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G). Since Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G) acts trivially on the center of GG, it follows that

(2.3) |Autc⁡(G)|≤Πi=1t​|xiG||\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)|\leq\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|x_{i}^{G}|

as there are only |xiG||x_{i}^{G}| choices for the image of each xix_{i} under any class-preserving automorphism. Since |xiG||x_{i}^{G}| is finite for each xix_{i}, 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t, it follows that |Autc⁡(G)|≤Πi=1t​|xiG||\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)|\leq\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|x_{i}^{G}| is finite.

We have proved the following result of which Theorem A is a corollary, because |G/Z⁡(G)|=|Inn⁡(G)|≤|Autc⁡(G)||G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\operatorname{Inn}(G)|\leq|\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)|.

Theorem 2.4.

Let GG be an arbitrary group such that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finitely generated by x1​Z⁡(G),x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G), x2​Z⁡(G),x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(G), …,xt​Z⁡(G)\ldots,x_{t}\operatorname{Z}(G) and the conjugacy class of xix_{i} in GG is of finite length for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Then Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G) is finite. Moreover |Autc⁡(G)|≤Πi=1t​|xiG||\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)|\leq\Pi_{i=1}^{t}|x_{i}^{G}| and γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite.

Proof of Theorem A is also reproduced using I​AIA-automorphisms (automorphisms of a group that induce identity on the abelianization) in [7, Theorem 2.3]. Proof goes on the same way as in the case of class-preserving automorphisms.

3. Groups with maximal central quotient

We start with the following concept due to Hall [8]. For a group XX, the commutator map aX:X/Z⁡(X)×X/Z⁡(X)→γ2​(X)a_{X}:X/\operatorname{Z}(X)\times X/\operatorname{Z}(X)\to\gamma_{2}(X) given by aX​(x1​Z⁡(X),x2​Z⁡(X))=[x1,x2]a_{X}(x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(X),x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(X))=[x_{1},x_{2}] is well defined. Two groups KK and HH are said to be isoclinic if there exists an isomorphism ϕ\phi of the factor group K¯=K/Z⁡(K)\bar{K}=K/\operatorname{Z}(K) onto H¯=H/Z⁡(H)\bar{H}=H/\operatorname{Z}(H), and an isomorphism θ\theta of the subgroup γ2​(K)\gamma_{2}(K) onto γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) such that the following diagram is commutative

K¯×K¯→aGγ2​(K)ϕ×ϕ↓↓θH¯×H¯→aHγ2​(H).\begin{CD}\bar{K}\times\bar{K}@>{a_{G}}>{}>\gamma_{2}(K)\\ @V{\phi\times\phi}V{}V@V{}V{\theta}V\\ \bar{H}\times\bar{H}@>{a_{H}}>{}>\gamma_{2}(H).\end{CD}

The resulting pair (ϕ,θ)(\phi,\theta) is called an isoclinism of KK onto HH. Notice that isoclinism is an equivalence relation among groups.

The following proposition (also see Macdonald’s result [14, Lemma 2.1]) is important for the rest of this section.

Proposition 3.1.

Let GG be a group such that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite. Then there exists a finite group HH isoclinic to the group GG such that Z⁡(H)≤γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)\leq\gamma_{2}(H). Moreover if GG is a pp-group, then HH is also a pp-group.

Proof.

Let GG be the given group. Then by Schur’s theorem γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite. Now it follows from a result of Hall [8] that there exists a group HH which is isoclinic to GG and Z⁡(H)≤γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)\leq\gamma_{2}(H). Since |γ2​(G)|=|γ2​(H)||\gamma_{2}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(H)| is finite, Z⁡(H)\operatorname{Z}(H) is finite. Hence, by the definition of isoclinism, HH is finite. Now suppose that GG is a pp-groups. Then it follows that H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) as well as γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) are pp-groups. Since Z⁡(H)≤γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)\leq\gamma_{2}(H), this implies that HH is a pp-group. □\Box

∎

For an arbitrary group GG with finite G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G), we have

(3.2) |G/Z⁡(G)|≤|γ2​(G)|d,|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d},

where d=d⁡(G/Z⁡(G))d=d(G/\operatorname{Z}(G)). For simplicity we say that a group GG has Property A if G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite and equality holds in (3.2) for GG. We are now going to classify, upto isoclinism, all groups GG having Property A.

Let GG be an arbitrary group having Property A. Then by Proposition 3.1 there exists a finite group HH isoclinic to GG and, by the definition of isoclinism, H has Property A. Thus for classifying all groups GG, upto isoclinism, having Property A, it is sufficient to classify all finite group with this property.

Let us first consider non-nilpotent finite groups. For such group we prove the following result in [5]

Theorem 3.3.

There is no non-nilpotent group GG having Property A.

So we only need to consider finite nilpotent groups. Since a finite nilpotent group is a direct product of it’s Sylow pp-subgroups, it is sufficient to classify finite pp-groups admitting Property A. Obviously, all abelian groups admit Property A. Perhaps the simplest examples of non-abelian groups having Property A are finite extraspecial pp-groups. The class of 22-generated finite capable nilpotent groups with cyclic commutator subgroup also admits Property A. A group GG is said to be capable if there exists a group HH such that G≅H/Z⁡(H)G\cong H/\operatorname{Z}(H). Isaacs [13, Theorem 2] proved: Let GG be finite and capable, and suppose that γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is cyclic and that all elements of order 44 in γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) are central in GG. Then |G/Z⁡(G)|≤|γ2​(G)|2|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{2}, and equality holds if GG is nilpotent. So GG admits Property A, if GG is a nilpotent group as in this statement and GG is 22-generated. A complete classification of 22-generated finite capable pp-groups of class 22 is given in [15].

Motivated by finite extraspecial pp-groups, a more general class of groups GG admitting Property A can be constructed as follows. For any positive integer mm, let G1,G2,…,GmG_{1},G_{2},\ldots,G_{m} be 22-generated finite pp-groups such that γ2​(Gi)=Z⁡(Gi)≅X\gamma_{2}(G_{i})=\operatorname{Z}(G_{i})\cong X (say) is cyclic of order qq for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, where qq is some power of pp. Consider the central product

(3.4) Y=G1∗XG2∗X⋯∗XGmY=G_{1}*_{X}G_{2}*_{X}\cdots*_{X}G_{m}

of G1,G2,…,GmG_{1},G_{2},\ldots,G_{m} amalgamated at XX (isomorphic to cyclic commutator subgroups γ2​(Gi)\gamma_{2}(G_{i}), 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m). Then |Y|=q2​m+1|Y|=q^{2m+1} and |Y/Z⁡(Y)|=q2​m=|γ2​(Y)|d⁡(Y)|Y/\operatorname{Z}(Y)|=q^{2m}=|\gamma_{2}(Y)|^{d(Y)}, where d⁡(Y)=2​md(Y)=2m is the number of elements in any minimal generating set for YY. Thus YY has Property A. Notice that in all of the above examples, the commutator subgroup is cyclic. Infinite groups having Property A can be easily obtained by taking a direct product of an infinite abelian group with any finite group having Property A.

We now proceed to showing that any finite pp-group GG of class 22 having Property A is isoclinic to a group YY defined in (3.4).

Let x∈Z2⁡(G)x\in\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G) for a group GG. Then, notice that [x,G][x,G] is a central subgroup of GG. We have the following simple but useful result.

Lemma 3.5.

Let GG be an arbitrary group such that Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finitely generated by x1​Z⁡(G),x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G), x2​Z⁡(G),…,xt​Z⁡(G)x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(G),\ldots,x_{t}\operatorname{Z}(G) such that e​x​p​([xi,G])exp([x_{i},G]) is finite for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Then

|Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)|=∏i=1te​x​p​([xi,G]).|\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=\prod_{i=1}^{t}exp([x_{i},G]).
Proof.

By the given hypothesis e​x​p​([xi,G])exp([x_{i},G]) is finite for all ii such that 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Suppose that e​x​p​([xi,G])=niexp([x_{i},G])=n_{i}. Since [xi,G]⊆Z⁡(G)[x_{i},G]\subseteq\operatorname{Z}(G), it follows that [xini,G]=[xi,G]ni=1[x_{i}^{n_{i}},G]=[x_{i},G]^{n_{i}}=1. Thus xini∈Z⁡(G)x_{i}^{n_{i}}\in\operatorname{Z}(G) and no smaller power of xix_{i} than nin_{i} can lie in Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}(G), which implies that the order of xi​Z⁡(G)x_{i}\operatorname{Z}(G) is nin_{i}. Since Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is abelian, we have |Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)|=∏i=1te​x​p​([xi,G])|\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=\prod_{i=1}^{t}exp([x_{i},G]). □\Box

∎

Let Φ⁡(X)\Phi(X) denote the Frattini subgroup of a group XX. The following result provides some structural information of pp-groups of class 22 admitting Property A.

Proposition 3.6.

Let HH be a finite pp-group of class 22 having Property A and Z⁡(H)=γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)=\gamma_{2}(H). Then

(i) γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) is cyclic;

(ii) H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) is homocyclic;

(iii) [x,H]=γ2​(H)[x,H]=\gamma_{2}(H) for all x∈H−Φ⁡(H)x\in H-\Phi(H);

(iv) HH is minimally generated by even number of elements.

Proof.

Let HH be the group given in the statement, which is minimally generated by dd elements x1,x2​…,xdx_{1},x_{2}\ldots,x_{d} (say). Since Z⁡(H)=γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)=\gamma_{2}(H), it follows that H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) is minimally generated by x1​Z⁡(H),x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(H), x2​Z⁡(H),…,xd​Z⁡(H)x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(H),\ldots,x_{d}\operatorname{Z}(H). Thus by the identity |H/Z⁡(H)|=|γ2​(H)|d|H/\operatorname{Z}(H)|=|\gamma_{2}(H)|^{d}, it follows that order of xi​Z⁡(H)x_{i}\operatorname{Z}(H) is equal to |γ2​(H)||\gamma_{2}(H)| for all 1≤i≤d1\leq i\leq d. Since the exponent of H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) is equal to the exponent of γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H), we have that γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) is cyclic and H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) is homocyclic. Now by Lemma 3.5, |γ2​(H)|d=|H/Z⁡(H)|=∏i=1te​x​p​([xi,H])|\gamma_{2}(H)|^{d}=|H/\operatorname{Z}(H)|=\prod_{i=1}^{t}exp([x_{i},H]). Since [xi,H]⊆γ2​(H)[x_{i},H]\subseteq\gamma_{2}(H), this implies that [xi,H]=γ2​(H)[x_{i},H]=\gamma_{2}(H) for each ii such that 1≤i≤d1\leq i\leq d. Let xx be an arbitrary element in H−Φ⁡(H)H-\Phi(H). Then the set {x}\{x\} can always be extended to a minimal generating set of HH. Thus it follows that [x,H]=γ2​(H)[x,H]=\gamma_{2}(H) for all x∈H−Φ⁡(H)x\in H-\Phi(H). This proves first three assertions.

For the proof of (iv), we consider the group H¯=H/Φ⁡(γ2​(H)){\bar{H}}=H/\Phi(\gamma_{2}(H)). Notice that both HH as well as H¯{\bar{H}} are minimallay generated by dd elements. Since [x,H]=γ2​(H)[x,H]=\gamma_{2}(H) for all x∈H−Φ⁡(H)x\in H-\Phi(H), it follows that for no x∈H−Φ⁡(H)x\in H-\Phi(H), x¯∈Z⁡(H¯){\bar{x}}\in\operatorname{Z}({\bar{H}}), where x¯=x​Φ​(γ2​(H))∈H¯{\bar{x}}=x\Phi(\gamma_{2}(H))\in{\bar{H}}. Thus it follows that Z⁡(H¯)≤Φ⁡(H¯)\operatorname{Z}({\bar{H}})\leq\Phi({\bar{H}}). Also, since γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) is cyclic, γ2​(H¯)\gamma_{2}({\bar{H}}) is cyclic of order pp. Thus it follows that H¯{\bar{H}} is isoclinic to a finite extraspecial pp-group, and therefore it is minimally generated by even number of elements. Hence HH is also minimally generated by even number of elements. This completes the proof of the proposition. □\Box

∎

Using the definition of isoclinism, we have

Corollary 3.7.

Let GG be a finite pp-group of class 22 admitting Property A. Then γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is cyclic and G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is homocyclic.

We need the following important result.

Theorem 3.8 ([3], Theorem 2.1).

Let GG be a finite pp-group of nilpotency class 22 with cyclic center. Then GG is a central product either of two generator subgroups with cyclic center or two generator subgroups with cyclic center and a cyclic subgroup.

Theorem 3.9.

Let GG be a finite pp-group of class 22 having Property A. Then GG is isoclinic to the group YY, defined in (3.4), for suitable positive integers mm and nn.

Proof.

Let GG be a group as in the statement. Then by Proposition 3.1 there exists a finite pp-group HH isoclinic to GG such that Z⁡(H)=γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)=\gamma_{2}(H). Obviously HH also satisfies |H/Z⁡(H)|=|γ2​(H)|d|H/\operatorname{Z}(H)|=|\gamma_{2}(H)|^{d}, where dd denotes the number of elements in any minimal generating set of G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G). Then by Proposition 3.6, γ2​(H)=Z⁡(H)\gamma_{2}(H)=\operatorname{Z}(H) is cyclic of order q=pnq=p^{n} (say) for some positive integer nn, and H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H) is homocyclic of exponent qq and is of order q2​mq^{2m} for some positive integer mm. Since Z⁡(H)=γ2​(H)\operatorname{Z}(H)=\gamma_{2}(H) is cyclic, it follows from Theorem 3.8 that HH is a central product of 22-generated groups H1,H2,…,HmH_{1},H_{2},\ldots,H_{m}. It is easy to see that γ2​(Hi)=Z⁡(Hi)\gamma_{2}(H_{i})=\operatorname{Z}(H_{i}) for 1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m and |γ2​(H)|=q|\gamma_{2}(H)|=q. This completes the proof of the theorem. □\Box

∎

We would like to remark that Theorem 3.9 is also obtained in [26, Theorem 11.2] as a consequence on study of class-preserving automorphisms of finite pp-group. But we have presented here a direct proof.

Now we classify finite pp-groups of nilpoency class larger than 22. Consider the metacylic groups

(3.10) K:=⟨x,y∣xpr+t=1,ypr=xpr+s,[x,y]=xpt⟩,K:=\left<x,y\mid x^{p^{r+t}}=1,y^{p^{r}}=x^{p^{r+s}},[x,y]=x^{p^{t}}\right>,

where 1≤t<r1\leq t<r and 0≤s≤t0\leq s\leq t (t≥2t\geq 2 if p=2p=2) are non-negative integers. Notice that the nilpotency class of KK is at least 33. Since KK is generated by 22 elements, it follows from (2.3) that |Autc⁡(K)|≤|γ2​(K)|2=p2​r|\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(K)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(K)|^{2}=p^{2r}. It is not so difficult to see that |Inn⁡(K)|=|K/Z⁡(K)|=p2​r|\operatorname{Inn}(K)|=|K/\operatorname{Z}(K)|=p^{2r}. Since Inn⁡(K)≤Autc⁡(K)\operatorname{Inn}(K)\leq\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(K), it follows that |Autc⁡(K)|=|Inn⁡(K)|=|γ2​(K)|2=|γ2​(K)|d⁡(K)|\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(K)|=|\operatorname{Inn}(K)|=|\gamma_{2}(K)|^{2}=|\gamma_{2}(K)|^{d(K)} (That Autc⁡(G)=Inn⁡(G)\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)=\operatorname{Inn}(G), is, in fact, true for all finite metacylic pp-groups). Thus KK admits Property A. Furthermore, if HH is any 22-generator group isoclinic to KK, then it follows that HH admits Property A. For a finite pp-groups having Property A, there always exists a pp-group HH isoclinic GG such that |H/Z⁡(H)|=|γ2​(H)|d|H/\operatorname{Z}(H)|=|\gamma_{2}(H)|^{d}, where d=d⁡(H)d=d(H). The following theorem now classifies, upto isoclinism, all finite pp-groups GG of nilpotency class larger than 22 having Property A.

Theorem 3.11 (Theorem 11.3, [26]).

Let GG be a finite pp-group of nilpotency class at least 33. Then the following hold true.

(i) If |G/Z⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d}, where d=d⁡(G)d=d(G), then d⁡(G)=2d(G)=2;

(ii) If |γ2​(G)/γ3​(G)|>2|\gamma_{2}(G)/\gamma_{3}(G)|>2, then |G/Z⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d} if and only if GG is a 22-generator group with cyclic commutator subgroup. Furthermore, GG is isoclinic to the group KK defined in (3.10) for suitable parameters;

(iii) If |γ2​(G)/γ3​(G)|=2|\gamma_{2}(G)/\gamma_{3}(G)|=2, then |G/Z⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d} if and only if GG is a 22-generator 22-group of nilpotency class 33 with elementary abelian γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) of order 44.

It is clear that the groups GG occuring in Theorem 3.11(iii) are isoclinic to certain groups of order 3232. Using Magma (or GAP), one can easily show that such groups of order 32 are SmallGroup(32,k) for k=6,7,8k=6,7,8 in the small group library.

We conclude this section with providing some different type of bounds on the central quotient of a given group. If |γ2​(G)​Z⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)|=n|\gamma_{2}(G)\operatorname{Z}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=n is finite for a group GG, then it follows from [22, Theorem 1] that |G/Z2⁡(G)|≤n2​l​o​g2​n|G/\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)|\leq n^{2\;log_{2}n}. Using this and Lemma 3.5 we can also provide an upper bound on the size of G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) in terms of nn, the rank of Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) and exponents of certain sets of commutators (here these sets are really subgroups of GG) of coset representatives of generators of Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) with the elements of GG. This is given in the following theorem.

Theorem 3.12.

Let GG be an arbitrary group. Let |γ2​(G)​Z⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)|=n|\gamma_{2}(G)\operatorname{Z}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G)|=n is finite and Z2⁡(G)/Z⁡(G)\operatorname{Z}_{2}(G)/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finitely generated by x1​Z⁡(G),x2​Z⁡(G),…,xt​Z⁡(G)x_{1}\operatorname{Z}(G),x_{2}\operatorname{Z}(G),\ldots,x_{t}\operatorname{Z}(G) such that e​x​p​([xi,G])exp([x_{i},G]) is finite for 1≤i≤t1\leq i\leq t. Then

|G/Z⁡(G)|≤n2​l​o​g2​n​∏i=1te​x​p​([xi,G]).|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq n^{2\;log_{2}n}{\prod}_{i=1}^{t}exp([x_{i},G]).

4. Problems and Examples

Theorem B provides some conditions on a group GG under which G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) becomes finite. It is interesting to solve

Problem 1. Let GG be an arbitrary group. Provide a set 𝒞\mathcal{C} of optimal conditions on GG such that G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is finite if and only if all conditions in 𝒞\mathcal{C} hold true.

As we know that there is no finite non-nilpotent group GG admitting Property A. Since Inn⁡(G)≤Autc⁡(G)\operatorname{Inn}(G)\leq\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G), it is interesting to consider

Problem 2. Classify all non-nilpotent finite group GG such that |Autc⁡(G)|=|γ2​(G)|d|\operatorname{Aut}_{c}(G)|=|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{d}, where d=d⁡(G)d=d(G).

A much stronger result than Theorem 3.3 is known in the case when the Frattini subgroup of GG is trivial. This is given in the following theorem of Herzog, Kaplan and Lev [10, Theorem A] (the same result is also proved independently by Halasi and Podoski in [11, Theorem 1.1]).

Theorem 4.1.

Let GG be any non-abelian group with trivial Frattini subgroup. Then |G/Z⁡(G)|<|γ2​(G)|2|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|<|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{2}.

The following result with the assertion similar to the preceding theorem is due to Isaacs [13].

Theorem 4.2.

If GG is a capable finite group with cyclic γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) and all elements of order 44 in γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) are central in GG, then |G:Z(G)|≤|γ2(G)|2|G:Z(G)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{2}. Moreover, equality holds if GG is nilpotent.

So, there do exist nilpotent groups with comparatively small central quotient. A natural problem is the following.

Problem 3. Classify all finite pp-groups GG such that |G:Z(G)|≤|γ2(G)|2|G:Z(G)|\leq|\gamma_{2}(G)|^{2}.

Let GG be a finite nilpotent group of class 22 minimally generated by dd elements. Then it follows from Lemma 3.5 that |G/Z⁡(G)|≤∏i=1de​x​p​([xi,G])|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq{\prod}_{i=1}^{d}exp([x_{i},G]), which in turn implies

(4.3) |G/Z⁡(G)|≤|e​x​p​(γ2​(G))|d.|G/\operatorname{Z}(G)|\leq|exp(\gamma_{2}(G))|^{d}.

Problem 4. Classify all finite pp-groups GG of nilpotency class 22 for which equality holds in (4.3).

Now we discuss some examples of infinite groups with finite central quotient. The most obvious example is the infinite cyclic group. Other obvious examples are the groups G=H×𝒵G=H\times\mathcal{Z}, where HH is any finite group and 𝒵\mathcal{Z} is the infinite cyclic group. Non-obvious examples include finitely generated F​CFC-groups, in which conjugacy class sizes are bounded, and certain Cernikov groups. We provide explicit examples in each case. Let FnF_{n} be the free group on nn symbols and pp be a prime integer. Then the factor group Fn/(γ2​(Fn)p​γ3​(Fn))F_{n}/(\gamma_{2}(F_{n})^{p}\gamma_{3}(F_{n})) is the required group of the first type, where γ2(Fn)p=⟨up∣u∈γ2(Fn)⟩\gamma_{2}(F_{n})^{p}=\left<u^{p}\mid u\in\gamma_{2}(F_{n})\right>. Now let H=𝒵⁡(p∞)×AH=\mathcal{Z}(p^{\infty})\times A be the direct product of quasi-cyclic (Prüfer) group 𝒵⁡(p∞)\mathcal{Z}(p^{\infty}) and the cyclic group A=⟨a⟩A=\left<a\right> of order pp, where pp is a prime integer. Now consider the group G=H⋊BG=H\rtimes B, the semidirect product of HH and the cyclic group B=⟨b⟩B=\left<b\right> of order pp with the action by xb=xx^{b}=x for all x∈𝒵⁡(p∞)x\in\mathcal{Z}(p^{\infty}) and ab=a​ca^{b}=ac, where cc is the unique element of order pp in 𝒵⁡(p∞)\mathcal{Z}(p^{\infty}). This group is suggested by V. Romankov and Rahul D. Kitture through ResearchGate, and is a Cernikov group.

The following problem was suggested by R. Baer in [1].

Problem 5. Let AA be an abelian group and QQ be a group. Obtain necessary and sufficient conditions on A and GG so that there exists a group QQ with A≅Z⁡(G)A\cong\operatorname{Z}(G) and Q≅G/AQ\cong G/A.

This problem was solved by Baer himself for an arbitrary abelian group A and finitely generated abelian group G. Moskalenko [16] solved this problem for an arbitrary abelian group A and a periodic abelian group G. He [17] also solved this problem for arbitrary abelian group A and a non-periodic abelian group G such that the rank of G/t⁡(G)G/t(G) is 11, where t⁡(G)t(G) denotes the tortion subgroup of GG. If this rank is more than 11, then he solved the problem when AA is a torsion abelian group. For a given group QQ, the existence of a group GG such that Q≅G/Z⁡(G)Q\cong G/\operatorname{Z}(G) has been studied extensively under the theme ‘Capable groups’. However, to the best of our knowledge, Problem 5 has been poorly studied in full generality. Let us restate a special case of this problem in a little different setup. A pair of groups (A,Q)(A,Q), where AA is an arbitray abelian group and QQ is an arbitrary group, is said to be a capable pair if there exists a group GG such that A≅Z⁡(G)A\cong\operatorname{Z}(G) and Q≅G/Z⁡(G)Q\cong G/\operatorname{Z}(G). So, in our situation, the following problem is very interesting.

Problem 6. Classify capable pairs (A,Q)(A,Q), where AA is an infinite abelian group and QQ is a finite group.

Finally let us get back to the situation when GG is a group with finite γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) but infinite G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G). The well known examples of such type are infinite extraspecial pp-groups. Other class of examples can be obtained by taking a central product (amalgamated at their centers) of infinitely many copies of a 22-generated finite pp-group of class 22 such that γ2​(H)=Z⁡(H)\gamma_{2}(H)=\operatorname{Z}(H) is cyclic of order qq, where qq is some power of pp. Notice that both of these classes consist of groups of nilpotency class 22. Now if we take G=X×HG=X\times H, where XX is an arbitrary group with finite γ2​(X)\gamma_{2}(X) and HH is with finite γ2​(H)\gamma_{2}(H) and infinite H/Z⁡(H)H/\operatorname{Z}(H), then γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite but G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is infinite. So we can construct nilpotent groups of arbitrary class and even non-nilpotent group with infinite central quotient and finite commutator subgroup.

A non-nilpotent group GG is said to be purely non-nilpotent if it does not have any non-trivial nilpotent subgroup as a direct factor. With the help of Rahul D. Kitture, we have also been able to construct purely non-nilpotent groups GG such that γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite but G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is infinite. Let HH be an infinite extra-special pp-group. Then we can always find a field ℱq\mathcal{F}_{q}, where qq is some power of a prime, containing all ppth roots of unity. Now let KK be the special linear group s​l​(p,ℱq)sl(p,\mathcal{F}_{q}), which is a non-nilpotent group having a central subgroup of order pp. Now consider the group GG which is a central product of HH and KK amalgamated at Z⁡(H)\operatorname{Z}(H). Then GG is a purely non-nilpotent group with the required conditions. It will be interesting to see more examples of this type which do not occur as a central product of such infinite groups of nilpotency class 22 with non-nilpotent groups.

By Proposition 2.2 we know that for an arbitrary group GG with finite γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) but infinite G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G), the group G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) has an infinite abelian group as a direct factor. Further structural information is highly welcome.

Problem 7. Provide structural information of the group GG such that γ2​(G)\gamma_{2}(G) is finite but G/Z⁡(G)G/\operatorname{Z}(G) is infinite?
